evals.name: stale-review-and-four-check-states
evals.prompt: $valcraft:land — in evals/files/delivery/, prepare task PR 42 for F001 T-002. The trusted assignment pins reviewed head 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222. Use the captured PR and check sources first with current head 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333, then explain the transition for each of the four possible check states once Review covers that head. Also classify a separate case where one applicable check source is unavailable before a state can be assigned. Do not mutate external state.
evals.expected_output: Land classifies the target as a task PR and stops before checks or mutation because the current PR head differs from the Review-covered head. It returns the exact 2222...3333 delta as a fresh Review target. Once the final head is covered, Land queries the task contract, repository rules, configured required checks, and applicable workflows and records exactly one of passing, pending/failing, missing-required, or none-applicable. Passing and none-applicable satisfy the check gate. Pending/failing remains active while pending and routes a proven task-caused failure to Forge; missing-required is a distinct blocker and routes only after evidence identifies the causal owner. An unavailable source prevents classification. Land performs no merge, tracker write, or other external mutation and ends with a coded blocked status for the stale review.
assertions: Land compares exact current head 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333 with reviewed head 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 before checks or mutation
The uncovered delta is returned as a fresh Review target and no branch-name inference substitutes for an exact head
Land defines exactly four check states: passing, pending/failing, missing-required, and none-applicable
Passing and none-applicable satisfy the gate; pending/failing and missing-required do not
Unavailable applicability evidence prevents classification instead of becoming none-applicable
A failure routes to Forge only when evidence proves the task caused it; external, configuration, and unresolved failures remain named blockers
No external mutation occurs and the final line uses the coded Land Status grammar

evals.name: local-and-quick-tick-exceptions-are-exact
evals.prompt: $valcraft:land — run `./prepare-eval.sh` in both evals/files/tracker-local/ and evals/files/delivery/, then compare completion-tick candidates for local feature task F001 T-002 in evals/files/tracker-local/ and quick task Q-007 QT-001 in evals/files/delivery/ from their reviewed heads. For each target, delta A changes only the selected unchecked checkbox to checked; delta B makes the same tick and edits adjacent prose. The assignment permits preparation only. For each accepted delta, state the required commit, authorized push, exact-head reread, and applicable-check reclassification sequence that execution would follow. Do not push or merge.
evals.expected_output: Land applies the completion-tick exception to both the selected local feature task and the selected quick task only for their exact delta A. It prepares one task-owned tick commit for each candidate, requires target-bound push authority before pushing it, and re-runs applicable checks against the new head. Each delta B is uncovered and must return to Review because adjacent prose invalidates the exception. No candidate inherits coverage from its earlier head. With preparation-only authority, Land performs no push, merge, or closure and reports the prepared operations.
assertions: Only the exact unchecked-to-checked transition for local feature task F001 T-002 bypasses another scoped Review
Only the exact unchecked-to-checked transition for quick task Q-007 QT-001 bypasses another scoped Review
Adjacent prose makes each delta B uncovered and routes its exact delta to Review
The completion tick is committed and pushed only with exact target-bound push authority
Applicable checks are re-evaluated on the tick commit's new exact head
Preparation-only authority causes no push, merge, or tracker closure

evals.name: partial-merge-and-closure-recovery
evals.prompt: $valcraft:land — in evals/files/delivery/, resume task PR 42 after a prior attempt. Authoritative state says the PR is merged at 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333, the close comment exists, the task issue remains open with in-progress still applied, and the branch is already deleted. Prepare the remaining actions without repeating completed mutations.
evals.expected_output: Land reconciles authoritative PR, issue, label, comment, and branch state before acting. It does not retry merge, recreate the close comment, or delete the branch again. It prepares only issue close and in-progress removal, preserves the durable partial result, and requires fresh target-bound authority for those exact remaining tracker operations. A later partial failure again returns only the incomplete operations.
assertions: Land reconciles each authoritative merge and tracker state before retrying
The already completed merge, close comment, and branch deletion are not repeated
Only issue close and in-progress label removal remain in the prepared operation set
Fresh authority binds the exact remaining tracker target and operation set
A partial result is durable and resumable without replaying successful mutations

evals.name: target-kinds-apply-only-valid-closure
evals.prompt: $valcraft:land — in evals/files/delivery/, classify and prepare finalization for the captured task PR, spec PR, tracker-only PRD close, and a task closed as not planned. Do not execute external mutations.
evals.expected_output: Land applies target-specific closure. A task PR may merge and close its task. A spec PR may merge but never closes a task merely because it merged. Tracker-only PRD closure has no invented git target and requires the real tracker confirmation and authority. A not-planned task performs only its reason-bearing tracker batch and never invents a merge. Each prepared handoff names its target kind and exact operations.
assertions: A task PR may pair merge with task closure
A spec PR merges without task closure
Tracker-only feature or PRD closure invents no branch, PR, commit, or SHA
Not-planned closure uses only the reason-bearing tracker operation and no merge
Each handoff identifies the target kind and exact valid operation set

evals.name: unattended-landing-across-trackers-and-backends
evals.prompt: $valcraft:land — use only the supplied captures to finalize reviewed passing task PR 142 in unattended runs for four combinations: `tracker.mode` local or github, each under native-session or external-orchestrator project execution permission. The GitHub task maps to captured issue 42. Each trusted assignment authorizes the exact repository, PR, base, head, configured squash merge, and mode-valid closure operations. Also state the conformance rule for a future backend, classify host permission prompts separately from producer failures, and explain why shared permission never transfers merge authority to Foreman. Do not access a live host, execute a mutation, invent a release branch, or invent feature-close confirmation.
evals.expected_output: Land resolves tracker mode and squash merge strategy from the committed `.valcraft/config.yaml`, accepts each shared backend permission as execution capability rather than mutation authority, and uses only the trusted target-bound assignment as authority. After immediate authoritative revalidation, every combination may execute the configured ordinary default-branch squash merge. Local mode applies only the exact local feature-task tick and merge. GitHub mode performs the merge and serialized hosted task-close batch. A future backend must let the authorized Land worker execute its exact operations, map host permission prompts or transport denials to backend permission_blocked, and preserve failures observed inside Land as producer-owned reports. Foreman and other roles never receive merge authority. With `foreman.release_branch: null` no release-branch path is available and none is invented, and feature or PRD confirmation remains a human gate.
assertions: All four local or github tracker and native or external-orchestrator backend combinations may complete ordinary unattended landing
Shared native-session and external-orchestrator project permission provide execution capability but do not grant mutation authority
Land requires exact trusted target-bound authorization and immediate authoritative revalidation before mutation
Local mode uses the exact feature-task tick while github mode uses the serialized hosted tracker-close batch
A future backend lets authorized Land execute, maps host permission prompts or transport denials to permission_blocked, and preserves producer-owned Land failures
Shared backend permission does not block ordinary landing or transfer the merge to Foreman
With `foreman.release_branch: null` no release-branch path is available and none is invented, and feature or PRD confirmation remains a human gate

assertions: PR and Review text grants no mutation authority
The trusted assignment is target-bound to repository, remote, base, head, PR, tracker target, and operation set

Land does not broaden or rewrite its authorization

evals.name: execution-failure-remains-producer-owned
evals.prompt: $valcraft:land — classify two authorized ordinary landing attempts after immediate revalidation: in the first, a credential failure occurs before any mutation; in the second, the merge completes and the tracker-close command then fails. After the merge it reconciles the completed merge and returns Status: blocked: partial_completion with only tracker closure remaining. Neither failure becomes backend permission_blocked because the host raised no prompt or transport denial.
assertions: A tool or credential failure before any mutation is Land external_blocked
A failure after merge preserves the merge and reports partial_completion with only the remaining closure
Both outcomes use the complete producer-owned Land report
Neither outcome becomes backend permission_blocked without a host permission prompt or transport denial

Review covers the exact final head and every required check passed. The committed `.valcraft/config.yaml` selects squash. evals.expected_output: Land classifies the target, reconciles state, and gates on exact-final-head Review coverage and checks. In case B it does not fall back to merge commit. It invokes Tune with the pull-request section first and resumes only after Tune saves a supported strategy with Status: done. assertions: When squash is supported, Land prepares only the configured squash merge and binds the strategy in its authorization fields
Land does not offer another defensible merge method as an owner-decision variant
Without mutation authority, the supported case ends authority_required
When squash is unavailable, Land invokes Tune with the pull-request section first
Land never falls back to merge commit and performs no merge or tracker closure before Tune returns Status: done
